name: Fuzzy answer match
summary: Does a typed answer match an accepted one? Normalizes case, accents, punctuation and articles, checks aliases, then a Damerau-Levenshtein ratio, a token-set ratio, plural and stem folding, and optionally a phonetic key. Deterministic, no LLM.
when_to_use: Any typed or open answer: trivia, naming, guess the character, spelling with tolerance.
gaps_it_closes: typed_answer matches only exact text with a trailing-s fold

name: Native text field
summary: A native text field in the game runtime kit, so typing has spaces, numbers and autocorrect, and replays record the text. The engine already has text submit/change input sources; the phone and bot runtime do not show the field yet.
when_to_use: Typed answers longer than one word, numbers, names, free-text prompts; replaces the on-screen keyboard fragment for typing.
api: inputs.<name>.from: {"text": "submit" | "change", placeholder?, max_len?} with text {value}; presentation.text_field {x, y, w, h, size}
gaps_it_closes: typing only through the keyboard fragment grid
notes: runtime side lives in FacebookClone/Bubbles/Runtime/web/bubble-kit-microgame.js

name: Answer bank
summary: Server-side content step: for each prompt, the accepted answers with aliases and also_accept lists, written by Muse at build time and checked for duplicates and reach.
when_to_use: Open-answer games where many answers are right: name a…, list games, rare-answer trivia.

name: Rarity tiers
summary: Sorts each prompt's accepted answers into tiers (common, uncommon, rare, legendary) by how often people would give them, so rarer answers can score more.
when_to_use: Rare-answer trivia and any typed game that rewards obscure answers; feeds typed_answer's tier string.
api: rarity_tiers(answer_bank) -> per prompt "a,b,c|d,e|f|g" (most common tier first)

name: Question bank
summary: Server-side content step: themed questions with a difficulty rating, the right answer and plausible distractors, checked for one right answer and no repeats.
when_to_use: Quizzes and trivia that should ramp in difficulty or draw from a large themed pool.
api: question_bank({theme, count, difficulty: [lo, hi], choices}) -> [{q, answer, distractors[], difficulty}]

name: Level list
summary: Server-side content step: an ordered list of levels or puzzle boards for one mechanic, each checked solvable by a solver or bot, with rising difficulty.
when_to_use: Puzzle and platform games played as a sequence of hand-made-feeling levels.
api: level_list({type_id, count, difficulty_curve}) -> [{level, data, solution?, difficulty}]

name: Themed word list
summary: Server-side content step: a themed word list with lengths and filters (only dictionary words, a fixed length, no proper nouns), for word games.
when_to_use: Hidden-word guessing, word search, hangman-like and spelling games with a theme.

name: Web lookup
summary: When the catalog misses a named game, looks it up on Wikipedia and the named site, and has Muse write a candidate game_type (mechanic only, with source URLs), saved as learned.
when_to_use: A request names a game, site or format the catalog has no alias for, or retrieval scores are low.
api: lookup(name) -> {game_type (status learned), refs[]}; budget 8 s; on failure the job continues without it

name: Friend answers
aliases: how well do you know me
summary: Collects short answers or picks from specific friends or a Group (about themselves or each other) so a game can ask players to guess them.
when_to_use: Guess-your-friends and party games whose content is the players themselves.
api: POST answers per game and person; GET a game's collected answers for players
notes: needs a backend endpoint; not in backend/README.md yet

name: Async turns
summary: Turn-based play between friends on their own phones: the server stores the game state and whose move it is, and notifies the next player.
when_to_use: Board, word and strategy games played move by move over hours, not on one phone (that is the turns fragment).
api: create match {gameId, players}; submit move; get match state
notes: needs a backend endpoint; challenges today are score-only

name: Freehand drawing
summary: Captures a finger-drawn stroke as points the game can keep, show and score. Can be approximated today with pointer move input plus a poly node (256 points); there is no stroke recognition.
when_to_use: Drawing and tracing games, draw-a-path puzzles, doodle guessing.
api: approximation: inputs from {"pointer": "move"} pushing points to state; poly {points}

name: Share grid
summary: A spoiler-free result grid (rows of coloured squares) a player can share after a run. Microgames share score text only today.
when_to_use: Daily puzzles and word games whose result people post to compare.

name: Segment collision
summary: Collision against line segments and polylines (walls, ropes, laser beams, drawn lines). Physics and helpers cover circles and unrotated boxes only.
when_to_use: Bouncing off drawn lines, mazes with thin walls, lasers, slicing.

name: Joints and constraints
summary: Physics joints: ropes, hinges, springs and chains between bodies.
when_to_use: Swinging, rope cutting, ragdolls, bridges, cranes.

name: Rotated collision shapes
summary: Bodies that rotate and collide as rotated boxes or polygons, with angular velocity. Images can be drawn rotated, but physics and overlap tests are axis-aligned.
when_to_use: Stacking that topples, tumbling blocks, angled platforms, spinning obstacles.

name: Device sensors (tilt)
summary: Tilt, motion and shake from the phone's sensors as game inputs.
when_to_use: Tilt to roll a ball, tilt to steer, shake to roll dice.
notes: approximate tilt with player_drag or hold_buttons

name: Live multiplayer
summary: Two or more people playing the same game at the same time on their own phones.
when_to_use: Live duels, races and party games across phones.
notes: approximate with turns (one phone), ghost_score or score_challenge (async)

name: 3D
summary: Three-dimensional scenes and cameras. The engine is 2D only.
when_to_use: Requests that need real 3D; usually re-planned as top-down, side-on or layered 2D.
notes: the anatomy prompt names this gap "3d"; catalog ids must start with a letter

name: Voice input
summary: Spoken answers transcribed into the game as text input.
when_to_use: Say-the-answer trivia, singing or shouting games, accessibility.
notes: Muse has a transcription model (muse-voice-transcribe-1.0); nothing in the runtime records audio

name: Multi-touch
summary: More than one finger at a time. The engine tracks one pointer: a second press releases the first.
when_to_use: Two-thumb controls, two players on one screen at once, pinch gestures.
notes: approximate with alternating turns or one-thumb controls

name: Layered loop player
summary: Plays several sound loops at once, in sync, each with its own on/off and volume, so players can layer and mix them.
when_to_use: Ambient mixers, loop stations, layered band and beat games.
gaps_it_closes: only one music loop plays at a time
notes: today presentation.music loops one rendered WAV, and timers can retrigger synth notes as step loops (see step_grid)

name: Sound clip content
summary: Recorded or sampled sound clips as content (animal calls, instruments, spoken words, music snippets) for listen-and-answer games.
when_to_use: Name-that-sound, listening quizzes, instrument-by-ear.
gaps_it_closes: all sound is synthesized; no recorded clips
notes: original synth melodies work today (audio_clip_player). Real songs and recordings can't be copied into games

name: Real-time growth
summary: Game state that persists between runs and advances with real time, so a plant, pet or garden grows between daily visits.
when_to_use: Daily care, idle growth, shared gardens and streaks that last days.
gaps_it_closes: game state resets every run; nothing carries over between days
notes: needs per-player (or per-Group) saved state on the backend; saves today are likes. shared_progress carries only a Group's total score

name: Collection book
summary: A collection that fills across runs (fish caught, stickers found), shown as a book with blanks for what's missing.
when_to_use: Fishing, collecting and gacha-like cozy games.
notes: within one run it's plain list state; across runs it needs the same saved state as growth_timer

name: Spaced repetition
summary: Schedules each card's next review by how well it was remembered, across days.
when_to_use: Study and vocabulary games played daily.
notes: needs saved per-player state (see growth_timer)

name: Drag to reshape
summary: Dragging changes a surface under the finger: wiping fog, raking sand, shaping clay.
when_to_use: Calm tactile toys: wipe the window, rake the sand, shape the pot.
notes: approximate with a coarse grid() of values changed by pointer move and drawn as rects; fine detail needs a real surface

name: Shape match score
summary: Scores how close a drawn stroke is to a target shape (average distance between the stroke and target points).
when_to_use: Tracing, draw-from-memory, perfect-circle and calligraphy games.
notes: can be approximated in rules with map, min_of and dist over the points, within collection limits

name: Colour mixer
summary: Mixes amounts of base colours into a resulting colour and measures how close it is to a target swatch.
when_to_use: Colour matching and mixing puzzles.
gaps_it_closes: no builtin turns numbers into a colour string
notes: the mix is plain maths, but the result must become a '#RRGGBB' string; a hex digit lookup list in rules works around it

name: Fill a region
summary: Tap a closed region of a line drawing to fill it with the current colour.
when_to_use: Colouring books and colour-by-number with real pictures.
notes: works today when regions are grid_board cells (pixel_grid); free-form regions need region shapes as content plus poly fills

name: Toppling stack physics
summary: Pieces stack and can tip over: physics with rotation, so off-centre weight topples the stack.
when_to_use: Balance and stacking games where toppling is the drama.
notes: physics_world stacks unrotated boxes and circles (no tipping); the gold slice_drop_stacker and pass_play_stacker fake it with overhang rules

name: Map pin
summary: Tap a map to place a pin; the pin's position converts to map coordinates for scoring by distance.
when_to_use: Geography guessing and place-finding games.
notes: tapping and distance work today (pointer_input, dist); the map picture must be geographically accurate, which generated art can't promise

name: Map pin guess
summary: Shows a clue, the player pins a guess on a map, and the score falls with the distance from the true place.
when_to_use: Where-was-this-taken, find-the-country and place quizzes.
notes: same building blocks as map_pin plus place coordinates as content (map_geometry)

name: Place coordinates
summary: Latitude and longitude for the places in a game, so rules can report the distance and compass direction between a guess and the answer.
when_to_use: Distance-and-direction geography puzzles.
notes: the maths is shipped builtins (sin, cos, sqrt, atan2); the coordinates must come from a checked source, not from Muse's memory

name: Meaning-closeness ranking
summary: For a secret word, a ranked list of other words by how close their meaning is, written at build time, so guesses can be told how warm they are.
when_to_use: Guess-the-word-by-meaning daily puzzles.
api: planned: content list ranked by closeness; in-game index_of(ranked, guess) gives the rank
gaps_it_closes: no embeddings (Muse has no embeddings endpoint)
notes: a Muse-written ranking covers only the words it lists; guesses outside it read as cold

name: Picture set
summary: A set of themed pictures as game content (scenes, objects, places), one per round.
when_to_use: Picture puzzles, spot-the-shape, jigsaws, frame-reveal guessing.
gaps_it_closes: art roles are sprites for pieces, not a list of full pictures per round
notes: the art pipeline makes sprites with frames (image_assets); a sheet of full-screen pictures per round is untested

name: In-game image generation
aliases: make a picture from my prompt
summary: Generates a picture from a player's prompt during play.
when_to_use: Prompt-the-picture and describe-and-draw games.
gaps_it_closes: art is made once at build time, not during play
notes: muse-image-1.0 exists on the server, but games run offline and deterministically; a live call breaks replays and needs a server round trip

name: Image similarity
summary: Scores how similar two pictures are.
when_to_use: Match-the-picture games.
notes: no model or endpoint for it

name: Drawing recognizer
summary: Names what a drawing shows.
when_to_use: Draw-it-and-the-computer-guesses games.
notes: approximate with friends guessing (friend_pairing, vote_tally)

name: Written answer grader
summary: Grades a short written answer against key points with Muse after the run.
when_to_use: Explain-it-back and short-answer learning games.
gaps_it_closes: typed answers can only be matched, not judged
notes: a Muse call is not deterministic, so the grade must be stored with the run rather than replayed; fuzzy_match covers short answers

name: Track list
summary: A list of song titles and artists to choose from, for playlist and music-taste games (names only, no audio).
when_to_use: Playlist curating and music-taste voting.
notes: titles can come from web_lookup; choosing among them works with quiz or sort_bins

name: Text to speech
summary: Speaks a word or phrase aloud for the player to type or repeat.
when_to_use: Spelling bees, dictation and listening practice.
notes: Muse lists a transcription model but no speech model; the runtime only synthesizes tones

name: Microphone input
summary: Records sound from the microphone during a run.
when_to_use: Singing, humming, beatboxing and foley games.
notes: same gap as voice_input

name: Pitch detection
summary: Detects the pitch of a sung or played note from the microphone.
when_to_use: Sing-the-note and tuning games.
notes: needs mic_input first

name: Sound classifier
summary: Labels recorded sounds (kick, snare, clap).
when_to_use: Beatbox and sound-sorting games.
notes: needs mic_input first

name: Speech input
summary: Turns what the player says into text for checking.
when_to_use: Pronunciation and say-the-answer games.
notes: same gap as voice_input; muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 could do the server side

name: Song generation
summary: Composes a song with lyrics and style from a description.
when_to_use: Make-a-song creative games.
notes: games can compose synth melodies from notes (note_grid, audio_synth); there is no vocal or full-song generation

name: Video scene
summary: Plays a short video in the game.
when_to_use: Foley, dubbing and react-to-a-clip games.
notes: approximate with an animated sprite scene (image_assets frames)

name: Tilt input
summary: Phone tilt or shake as input.
when_to_use: Tilt to roll, shake to stir.
notes: same gap as device_sensors; approximate with drag or swipe

name: Flashlight beam
summary: The scene is dark except a beam or circle of light the player moves; only what's inside it is visible.
when_to_use: Dark exploration, horror and hide-and-seek.
gaps_it_closes: no masking or clipping in rendering
notes: approximate: draw objects only when dist to the light is under the radius, over a dark background; a true mask with soft edges needs engine support

name: Limited light
summary: A light radius that shrinks as its fuel runs down and resets when refuelled; only things inside it are shown.
when_to_use: Light-rationing horror and survival exploration.
gaps_it_closes: no masking or clipping in rendering
notes: same approximation as flashlight_mask, with the radius from a timer_bar

name: Vision cone
summary: Guards see in a cone; the player is spotted when inside a guard's cone and range, unless cover blocks the view.
when_to_use: Stealth games and sneaking puzzles.
notes: the cone test works in rules (angle, dist, atan2) and a poly can draw it; blocking by cover needs segment_collision

name: Directional sound
aliases: where is the sound coming from
summary: Plays a sound so it seems to come from a direction (left, right, behind).
when_to_use: Locate-the-sound games and audio horror.
notes: synth sounds have wave, pitch, length and volume but no pan; approximate direction with pitch or volume cues

name: Anomaly variants
summary: Builds versions of one scene where some have a small change (an object moved, recoloured or missing), with the answer recorded.
when_to_use: Spot-the-anomaly, what-changed and spot-the-difference rounds.
api: planned: a base scene as a list of placed objects plus per-round edits {object, change}
notes: works today if the scene is drawn from object lists in state (the changes are rule edits); changes inside one generated picture are not possible
